title: Staged hardware proforma — quantized workload split and lane sizing
summary: A staged proforma for Private/VPC fleet purchases that splits workloads into quantized lanes (latency-sensitive, mixed, and batch) and produces a hardware BOM with safety buffers and region allocations. Includes assumptions for quantization savings, batching multipliers, and per-GPU throughput so procurement can be phased across quarters.
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is intended to give a procurement-ready proforma for private/VPC inference fleets where workloads are intentionally split into 3 lanes:
  1) Latency lane (real-time chat, low concurrency, tight p99 SLOs)
  2) Mixed lane (interactive + small batch; moderate latency SLOs)
  3) Batch lane (embeddings, offline rerank, heavy quantization allowed)

Assumptions (global):
  - Planning horizon: 12 months, staged buys across Q1/Q2/Q3.
  - Safety buffer: default 25% headroom on top of computed steady-state capacity (configurable per scenario).
  - Typical request mix at t=0: 50% latency, 30% mixed, 20% batch. Growth scenarios below alter mix.
  - Quantization savings: latency lane uses int8 where possible (1.6x throughput), mixed lane uses int8/4 approx (2.4x for batchable ops), batch lane aggressively uses int4/4 with KV-cache reuse (3.2x).
  - Batching multipliers: latency lane effective batch size 1-4, mixed 4-16, batch 32-256.
  - Model targets: 13B and 70B classes. Throughput numbers below are tokens/sec for a single GPU on average-request profile (context ~1k tokens).

Per-GPU throughput (tokens/sec) baseline (unquantized):
  - H100-80: 700 tps (13B), 160 tps (70B)
  - A100-80: 520 tps (13B), 120 tps (70B)
  - L4-24: 380 tps (13B), 90 tps (70B)
  - T4-equivalent (edge): 110 tps (13B), 28 tps (70B)
Quantized effective throughput multipliers applied per lane above. Example: L4-24 on 13B in batch lane -> 380 * 3.2 = ~1216 tps.

sizing_notes:
Sizing method (high-level):
  1) Convert peak tokens/sec requirement into equivalent GPU-minutes using per-GPU effective tps (apply quantization multipliers by lane).
  2) Add safety buffer (default 25%) and convert to required GPU count.
  3) Map GPU count to server SKUs by preferred density (we prefer fewer SKUs: L4 for latency, A100 for mixed, H100 for dense batch).
  4) Phase buys across quarters: 40% phase1, 35% phase2, 25% phase3, adjustable by region and budget.
  5) Validate rack space, power, and network constraints — reserve 1.25x power headroom for thermal contingencies.

Example calculation (Expected, us-west):
  - Peak tokens/sec = 132k (from table).
  - Lane split: latency 50% => 66k tps, mixed 28% => 36.96k tps, batch 22% => 29.04k tps.
  - Choose GPU types: latency -> L4-24 (13B), mixed -> A100-80 (13B), batch -> H100-80 (70B heavy).
  - Effective tps after quantization:
    latency: 380 * 1.6 = 608 tps per L4 -> 66,000 / 608 = ~109 GPUs (round up 120 with buffer)
    mixed: 520 * 2.4 = 1,248 tps per A100 -> 36,960 / 1,248 = ~30 GPUs (round up 36)
    batch: 160 (H100 at 70B baseline) * 3.2 = 512 tps per GPU -> 29,040 / 512 = ~57 GPUs (round up 70)
  - Total GPUs = 120 + 36 + 70 = 226 GPUs -> map to servers per SKU and apply safety buffer and rackization.

Power and rack planning quick checks: average server power (fully loaded)
  - L4 node (4x L4): 1300W
  - A100 node (4x A100): 3200W
  - H100 dense (8x H100): 9000W
  - Include 25% spare PDU capacity planning

Procurement notes and options to reduce upfront spend:
  - Consider hybrid procurement: reserve 60% as owned BOM; 40% as dedicated cloud bursts for first 6 months to de-risk demand forecast.
  - Negotiate GPU warranty and RMA SLAs for private fleets; target 48-hour replacement SLA.
  - Test quantization profiles and offline evals on a 10-node pilot before large buy to validate quality delta (LLM output perf/regression).

Validation checklist before PO:
  - Pilot results: latency p99 under SLO for latency lane with chosen L4 + int8 stack.
  - Evals: quality drift < 2% on key prompt sets after quantization.
  - Monitoring: tracing hooks to attribute model variant and quantization level to error/latency.
  - Security: HSM/KMS integration tested for customer keys in private deployment.

Open questions for next sync:
  - Should APAC use more H100 density to reduce cross-region replication?
  - Is 25% safety buffer acceptable for enterprise SLAs or do customers demand more headroom?
  - Which vendors support 6-month payment terms without price step-ups?

notes:
Why this is different from other BOMs:
  - Focuses on lane-based procurement tied to quantization profiles (explicit multipliers) rather than a single utilization curve.
  - Emphasizes phased buys and hybrid cloud/owned mix as a procurement risk reduction strategy.
  - Includes clear, repeatable GPU->throughput math so SRE/Bench teams can re-run with updated per-model microbenchmarks.
